Maia for Media and publishing

Keep the sources, rights, and handoffs with the story.

Maia prepares editorial and production briefs from the records your team selects. Editors and producers retain responsibility for reporting, accuracy, rights, standards, and publication.

All industries ↗

Keep editorial evidence attached

Stories and productions move through pitches, research, source notes, drafts, assets, legal or standards review, and publication. Maia can prepare a shared brief in Slack that keeps claims connected to their sources and makes missing work visible.

Editors and producers decide what is accurate, fair, original, and ready to publish. Maia organizes the material around those decisions.

Build a research brief

Provide the assignment, approved notes, transcripts, source documents, and named web research. Ask Maia to separate verified facts, attributed claims, background, disputed points, and questions that still need reporting.

The brief should cite the exact source and access date where relevant. A summary does not replace source checking, and Maia should not manufacture a quote or collapse different speakers into one view.

Coordinate the production handoff

Give Maia the final assignment, draft status, asset list, format requirements, owners, and deadlines. It can prepare a checklist for copy, visuals, audio or video, captions, metadata, review, and publication.

The producer assigns the work and confirms the schedule. A missing asset or unclear specification remains a visible dependency instead of becoming a last-minute surprise.

Surface rights and attribution questions

Using the supplied asset register and editorial policy, Maia can flag items with missing ownership, license, credit, consent, or usage scope. It can also check that attributed claims in the draft point to the supplied notes.

The rights, legal, or editorial owner makes the determination. Maia does not claim that an asset is cleared simply because a file is available.

Prepare publication review

Before publication, Maia can compare the current draft with the assignment, fact-check notes, corrections, asset requirements, and channel-specific checklist. It can return unresolved claims and owners in one thread.

The editor gives final approval. Any publishing action remains separate from the review so a completed checklist does not automatically make content public.

Start with one finished assignment

Choose one story packet with source notes, a draft, and an image with incomplete rights metadata. Ask Maia to preserve attribution and identify the rights gap, then let the editor assign the reporting and rights follow-up.

After the editorial meeting, Maia can prepare the decision recap with assignments, source follow-ups, rights questions, and production dates. The editor can correct it in the thread, and each owner leaves with the exact record or asset they need to review.

For a recurring series, the team can reuse the same assignment and publication checklist while changing the story sources. That consistency helps producers spot missing work without making the editorial judgment formulaic.

Questions from media teams

Can Maia write an article or script?

It can draft from an approved brief and supplied evidence. Editors remain responsible for originality, accuracy, standards, and publication.

Does Maia verify usage rights?

It can compare supplied rights records with policy and flag missing information. A qualified owner confirms permission.

Can Maia publish content?

Begin with preparation and review. Any supported publishing action should show the exact destination and content to an authorized editor first.
